input: The strainer should be isolated before the cover is broken. The duty should first be transferred to the standby pump, and the discharge proved steady on the standby machine. The duty pump should then be stopped at its local starter and the isolation lock applied; the isolation is carried out under the PTW. The strainer inlet valve and the strainer outlet valve should be closed, and both should be proved shut by means of the drain. The strainer drain should be opened to its safe destination and the vent at the high point of the body should be opened. It should be emphasised that the strainer body will hold stored pressure even after the valves have been closed, and the body should accordingly be proved drained, vented, and at zero pressure before any flange is loosened; the closed valves alone should not be relied upon as this proof. The cleaning itself takes about 82 min with the unit isolated, and the isolation is held for the whole of that period: the duty pump remains locked out, the standby pump carries the service, and the drain is left open to catch any passing at the inlet valve. The strainer should be handed back only when the cleaning is complete and the cover remade, with the return to service following the reverse of the isolation and the body being filled and vented before the duty pump is restarted.
